pattern_title: IN DSNP HMO spend is trapped in a massive Not Mapped bucket
pattern_description: IN DSNP HMO spend is heavily concentrated in a Not Mapped facility bucket, adding about $66.0M. Claim volume also increased materially, but because the facility classification is missing, it is not possible to tell whether the change reflects true utilization growth, a site-of-care shift, or a mapping problem. This should be treated as a gating validation issue before broader authorization, reimbursement, or network actions are taken in IN DSNP HMO.

rows.maternity_bundling: Global obstetrical care is bundled once per pregnancy, including routine prenatal, delivery, and postpartum care.
rows.delivery_claim_requirements: Clinical review determines related readmissions; delivery claims need outcome/gestation codes, documentation, and pregnancy limits.

individual_policies.evidence: This policy does not map to a specific DRG code; it applies to inpatient readmission adjudication for DRG-reimbursed facilities. Unplanned readmissions within 30 days for the same, similar, or related condition are not separately reimbursed, and planned readmissions or leave of absence cases are treated as one admission with one DRG payment.

No explicit DRG mapping appears; maternity services are adjudicated under global obstetrical billing rules, duplicate or overlapping maternity claims may be denied or recouped, and multiple state Medicaid exceptions apply.

individual_policies.policy_title: Coding Edits Policy (Commercial, Medicare, and Medicaid)
individual_policies.evidence: EmblemHealth denies HCPCS C-code claims when they are billed outside the allowed facility bill types or when they are billed on professional claims.

The only explicitly addressed outpatient temporary HCPCS code is G0500. It is allowed when the same physician or other qualified health care professional performing a gastrointestinal endoscopic procedure also provides the initial 15 minutes of moderate sedation, with additional time reportable using 99153 when appropriate. The policy does not state a broader edit for unattributed outpatient temporary-code spend beyond this code-specific rule.

This payer recognizes modifier 52 on outpatient facility and professional claims for partially reduced services, and reimburses the line at a reduced fee schedule amount when documentation supports the reduction. The modifier cannot be used with several code or modifier combinations and is not valid for time-based codes or maternity delivery codes.

The plan recognizes office E&M visits with modifier TH for antepartum care when fewer than 4 antepartum visits were rendered. TH is limited to antepartum visits 1-3, is not used for postpartum E&M visits, and cannot be billed by the same provider or provider group that bills global maternity care.

General modifier-payment policy for Medicare Advantage claims. It requires CPT and HCPCS modifiers only when appropriate, reviews modifier-code combinations, and may deny or recover payment for incorrect modifier use. No specific rule for unattributed outpatient temporary-code spend is stated.

pattern_title: TX acute hospital spend is being driven by a handful of very high-cost IP Med/Surg cases
pattern_description: TX DSNP HMO acute hospital spend is being pushed by a small set of very high-cost IP Med/Surg cases rather than broad-based utilization growth. The pattern centers on pancreatic disorders, pulmonary embolism, complex lower-extremity procedures, and inflammatory bowel disease, with several single-case increases near $0.2M. Some of the clinical records also show null or blank procedure fields, so case review and data validation should occur together.

individual_policies.evidence: General inpatient provider-preventable-condition policy. For inpatient facility claims, POA indicators are required, HCAC-related charges and days are removed from DRG payment, and wrong-body-part, wrong-patient, or wrong-surgery events are denied or rejected. No code-specific rule for the analyzed code.
